correctness.rationale: Triple XOR on distinct indexed columns is exactly evaluation on the queries; columns themselves can repeat. Only full-rank matrices can shatter or reach 63 at d=6. I independently enumerated kernels by the jumps of their highest-bit filtration and counted covered cosets by bitset translation unions. All seven Gaussian-binomial counts and full trace distributions matched. In particular, 788035 nine-coordinate three-planes yield the claimed maximum of 63 and the same set of 2304 extremizers. Generator-column multiplicities up to GL(3,2) independently recover their four S9 orbits of sizes 1260, 756, 252 and 36 and verify the named representatives. Direct triple XOR verifies the four covering witnesses and the near-cover witness. Padding and the bound of 56 hypotheses at eight coordinates complete the minimality claims.
residual_risks: Exact finite results only, on static queries for weight exactly three; the 2304 count is of kernels, not named matrices.

value.rationale: This is an exact additive-covering problem intrinsic to a fixed-weight learning class. The cardinality lower bound would allow nine coordinates for six queries, but the algebraic obstruction forces ten. The classification identifies all ways to get the best near-cover, rather than showing a gap by examples alone.
residual_risks: No asymptotic or adaptive consequence established.
